blog-minecraft-server-meta-description: How I run my private Minecraft server: Paper-optimized or as a custom modpack, in Docker, with secured access plus RAID-1 and cron backups.
blog-minecraft-server-heading: Self-Hosted Minecraft Server: Docker, VPN & Backups
blog-minecraft-server-section-1-title: Why Run My Own Minecraft Server?
blog-minecraft-server-section-1-text: I run my Minecraft server myself to have full control over the game environment, security, and performance. It runs on my own hardware. Self-hosting lets me decide who gets access and tune the configuration exactly to each group of players.
blog-minecraft-server-section-2-text: Depending on the occasion, the server runs in one of two variants: as a Paper server with an optimized configuration for smooth, resource-friendly gameplay, or as a fully custom modpack whose mods and configuration I put together and tune myself.
blog-minecraft-server-section-3-text: The server runs inside a Docker container. This isolates the environment from the rest of the system and simplifies maintenance, updates, and switching between different setups.
blog-minecraft-server-section-4-text: Players connect through an OpenVPN network, so the server needs no direct port forwarding to the internet. All connections are encrypted and secured with my own certificates, so only players with a valid certificate can reach the server at all.
blog-minecraft-server-section-5-text: The server runs on Linux, with its data stored on a RAID-1 that protects against a disk failure. In addition, cron jobs back up the worlds automatically, so saves stay recoverable even after errors or failed updates.
